title: Découvrir les mots
oneGoal: Students recognize that French has words we can discover and explore
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students with French sounds?
What visual supports do they need for comprehension?
Should we use more gestures and TPR?
progression: Builds the foundation for all word exploration activities
realWorldConnection: People use words to communicate every day in French

title: Sons et lettres
oneGoal: Students connect French sounds to letters they can see
decisionPoints: Are students making sound-letter connections?
Do they need more auditory repetition?
Should we focus on specific sounds causing difficulty?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by connecting the abstract concept of 'mots' to concrete sounds and letters
realWorldConnection: Reading signs, labels, and books requires knowing letter sounds

title: Familles de sons
oneGoal: Students group words that start with the same sound
decisionPoints: Can students hear the beginning sounds clearly?
Do they need more physical sorting activities?
Should we reduce the number of sound families?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by organizing individual sounds into patterns and families
realWorldConnection: Grouping similar things helps us organize our thoughts and learning

title: Jeu des rimes
oneGoal: Students recognize words that sound similar at the end (rhymes)
decisionPoints: Are students hearing the rhyming patterns?
Do they need more movement-based rhyming activities?
Should we use familiar songs or chants?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by extending sound families to include ending sounds and rhymes
realWorldConnection: Rhymes help us remember songs, poems, and make language fun

title: Mots courts et longs
oneGoal: Students compare and categorize words by their length
decisionPoints: Can students visually see the difference in word length?
Do they need hands-on measuring activities?
Should we use clapping to count syllables?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by adding visual analysis to sound analysis of words
realWorldConnection: Long and short words appear in books, signs, and everyday writing

title: Syllabes et battements
oneGoal: Students identify syllables by clapping word parts
decisionPoints: Are students successfully clapping syllables?
Do they need more kinesthetic practice?
Should we focus on 1-2 syllable words first?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by breaking long words into manageable parts
realWorldConnection: Breaking words into parts helps us read and spell new words

title: Petits mots magiques
oneGoal: Students recognize high-frequency words that appear everywhere
decisionPoints: Which high-frequency words are students ready for?
Do they need more visual word cards or games?
Should we focus on word recognition or spelling?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by introducing words that appear frequently in French reading
realWorldConnection: These 'magic words' help us read books, signs, and messages faster

title: Construire des mots
oneGoal: Students build new words by combining letters and sounds
decisionPoints: Are students able to blend sounds successfully?
Do they need more letter manipulation practice?
Should we use magnetic letters or letter tiles?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by actively creating words instead of just recognizing them
realWorldConnection: Writers create new words by putting letters and sounds together

title: Mots de la même famille
oneGoal: Students find words that belong to the same word family
decisionPoints: Can students see the patterns in word families?
Do they need more visual sorting activities?
Should we focus on one word family at a time?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by organizing constructed words into meaningful groups
realWorldConnection: Word families help us predict how to read and spell similar words

title: Chasse aux mots
oneGoal: Students search for and identify specific words in text
decisionPoints: Are students successfully locating target words?
Do they need highlighted text or word frames?
Should we use familiar books or simple sentences?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by applying word recognition skills to actual reading materials
realWorldConnection: We search for specific words when reading recipes, instructions, or finding information

title: Inventer avec les mots
oneGoal: Students create simple sentences using their word knowledge
decisionPoints: Are students ready to combine words into sentences?
Do they need sentence frames or word banks?
Should we focus on oral or written creation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by using found words to create meaningful communication
realWorldConnection: We combine words to share our thoughts, feelings, and ideas with others

title: Mes mots préférés
oneGoal: Students choose and justify their favorite French words
decisionPoints: Can students explain why they like certain words?
Do they need support with opinion language?
Should we use drawings or gestures to help explanations?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by encouraging personal connection and reflection on word learning
realWorldConnection: Having favorite words makes reading and writing more personal and enjoyable

title: Dictionnaire d'images
oneGoal: Students organize their learned words into a visual dictionary
decisionPoints: How should students organize their word collection?
Do they need help with alphabetical order or categories?
Should we use digital tools or paper-based organization?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by formally organizing and documenting word learning
realWorldConnection: Dictionaries help us find and remember words when reading and writing

title: Présentation de mes découvertes
oneGoal: Students share their word discoveries with classmates
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students presenting in French?
Do they need presentation supports or sentence starters?
Should presentations be individual or in pairs?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by demonstrating mastery through teaching others
realWorldConnection: Sharing what we learn helps others and strengthens our own understanding

title: Jeux de mots créatifs
oneGoal: Students play creative word games for enjoyment and practice
decisionPoints: Which word games engage students most effectively?
Do they need new games or variations of familiar ones?
Should games be competitive or collaborative?
progression: Extends Lesson 14 by applying word knowledge in playful, low-pressure contexts
realWorldConnection: Playing with words makes language learning fun and memorable

title: Histoires avec nos mots
oneGoal: Students create simple stories using their vocabulary collection
decisionPoints: Are students ready for story creation?
Do they need story frames or picture prompts?
Should stories be oral, written, or illustrated?
progression: Extends Lesson 15 by combining word play with narrative creation
realWorldConnection: Stories help us share experiences and connect with others

title: Mots dans notre école
oneGoal: Students identify and collect French words around the school environment
decisionPoints: Which school areas have the most accessible French words?
Do students need recording sheets or cameras?
Should this be done in small groups or as a class?
progression: Extends Lesson 16 by connecting vocabulary learning to their immediate environment
realWorldConnection: French words surround us in our daily environment at school and beyond

title: Atelier de poésie simple
oneGoal: Students create simple poems using their favorite words and sounds
decisionPoints: Are students comfortable with creative expression?
Do they need poetry templates or complete freedom?
Should poems focus on rhyme, rhythm, or meaning?
progression: Extends Lesson 17 by using environmental words in artistic expression
realWorldConnection: Poetry helps us express feelings and appreciate the beauty of language

title: Concours d'orthographe amical
oneGoal: Students participate in a friendly spelling celebration of learned words
decisionPoints: How can we make spelling fun and non-threatening?
Should we use team formats or individual challenges?
Do we need different difficulty levels for different students?
progression: Extends Lesson 18 by celebrating spelling achievement in a supportive atmosphere
realWorldConnection: Correct spelling helps others understand our writing clearly

title: Célébration des explorateurs
oneGoal: Students celebrate their journey as word explorers and plan future learning
decisionPoints: How should we recognize each student's growth?
What celebration format would be most meaningful?
How can we connect this to continued French learning?
progression: Extends Lesson 19 by reflecting on the complete learning journey and looking forward
realWorldConnection: Celebrating our learning motivates us to continue growing and exploring
